content:
deploy-bot: Hotfix candidate built and pushed: gcr.io/redwood-inference/routing-agent:hotfix-20260323-0ab9f
deploy-bot: Canary started in dedicated-pool-us-east-1 (5% traffic). Monitoring window 10m. Link: https://console.redwood/inference/releases/0ab9f

nora: seeing customer reports of stalled requests ~5m ago, thanks for the quick turnaround. :pray:

tim: can we get expedited roll to 100%? impact on a few committed Dedicated customers.

sylvia: what are the canary metrics currently?
deploy-bot: Current snapshot (1m window):
```
canary_errors: 0.8%
canary_p95_latency: 850ms
canary_qps: 420
open_connections_avg: 78
cpu: 62%
mem_rss: 4.2GB
```

ops-lead: I need a clear rollback trigger before we go +1. Propose: rollback if errors > 1.5% sustained for 3m OR p95 > 1.2s for 5m OR server restarts > 2 in 10m.

release-manager: Confirming expedited approval flow: we need ops-lead +1 and devops +1, then I can sign the release note and unblock deploybot.

devops: I reviewed the artifact diff — small change to connection pooling and a guard for event-loop stalls. Looks sane. +1.

oncall-aaron: I'm on pager, can monitor metrics and execute rollback if necessary. +1 from oncall.

ops-lead: +1 from me. Given committed customers are affected, I'm okay with fast-track. Ops will hold the rollback playbook ready. :white_check_mark:

release-manager: All approvals present. Noting release note stub: https://docs.internal/releases/2026-03-23-routing-hotfix (I'll add emails after rollout).

nora: calling out migration note — this image flips a connection cap from 1000->500 which reduces bursty spikes. Verified in staging.

devops: Kicking the rollout. Command:```/deploy canary --service routing-agent --image gcr.io/redwood-inference/routing-agent:hotfix-20260323-0ab9f --canary 5% --duration 10m```

deploy-bot: Canary in progress -> 5% traffic. Observing.

(deploy-bot automated update) 3271112240: canary metrics: errors 0.9%, p95 870ms, restarts 0

nora: checking logs — connection timeout traces down 70% vs last hour. Good signal.

tim: recommend ramp to 30% for 5m then 100% if green. ops?

ops-lead: agree. Ramp to 30% then evaluate against rollback criteria.

devops: Running ramp command now: ```/deploy ramp --service routing-agent --to 30% --wait 5m```

(deploy-bot automated update) 3271112260: ramp to 30% started. Metrics will be posted in channel.

(deploy-bot automated update) 3271112270: ramp snapshot: errors 0.95%, p95 900ms, restarts 0

oncall-aaron: monitoring dashboards, will call rollback at first sign of sustained breach.

release-manager: I'm posting release notes and informing customer success for the affected Dedicated customers. Draft note: "Routing agent hotfix: connection pooling tuning to mitigate stalled requests for dedicated pools. Rolling now."

devops: Criteria met to proceed to 100%. Executing: ```/deploy promote --service routing-agent --to 100%```

deploy-bot: Promotion started -> routing-agent at 100% for dedicated-pool-us-east-1. Expected full cutover in ~2m.

(deploy-bot automated update) 3271112280: rollout complete. Final check: errors 0.7%, p95 780ms, restarts 0. All green.

ops-lead: Nice work team. Keeping the rollback playbook open for 30m of post-deploy watch.

nora: Thanks everyone. I'll open an ops postmortem doc if anything resurfaces, otherwise will archive notes. :thumbsup:
